headings.text: Designated service lifetime under Deploy App 2.x

blocks.html:
Security is a first-class goal for Deploy App ("Security and quality first"). This page covers how to report vulnerabilities privately, the supported-versions / design-lifetime expectations, and the CA/trust posture that differs between the legacy and Kubernetes stacks.

Reporting a vulnerability

Do not open a public GitHub issue for a security problem. Report it privately so it can be triaged and fixed before disclosure.

Not yet documented. The private vulnerability-reporting channel for the pvarki org (GitHub private vulnerability reporting or a security mailbox) is still being set up; the exact address and process will be linked here once it is in place. Until then, do not file security issues in public trackers.

When reporting, include the affected stack and version/tag (and the submodule set for the legacy stack), reproduction steps, and the impact you observed.

Supported versions under Deploy App 2.x

We, presently, only support the latest version tag of [(https://github.com/pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-integration/tags)] and latest version tags of each of our components

Designated service lifetime under Deploy App 2.x

A Deploy App deployment is intended to be short-lived. The legacy README states a design lifetime of 1–2 months and warns explicitly against running a single deployment longer:

If you wish to use one deployment for longer than the design lifetime of 1–2 months you can change the following env variables. But do understand that this is not recommended and has security implications.

The relevant knobs are the CFSSL certificate expiries, which default to short windows:

CFSSL_CA_EXPIRY="hours here"
CFSSL_SIGN_DEFAULT_EXPIRY="hours here, make sure it equals CFSSL_CA_EXPIRY"

The README is blunt about the tradeoff: if you extend the lifetime, you take responsibility to go through all Dockerfiles and compositions and apply security updates yourself. The supported, secure path is to stand up a fresh deployment from a current tag rather than nurse an old one. Tearing down with docker compose down -v deletes certificates and all user state — treat that as a full reset, not an upgrade step.

The upcoming OpenDefence k8s-platform deployment model may change the designated service lifetime of a Deploy App instance.

\nWe only alter this when we have designed and enforced methods for service operators to both keep their services up-to-date AND enabled certificate / ID lifecycle refreshing within Deploy App, in order to ensure high security of a Deploy App service.

Supply-chain scanning

CI enforces dependency and image scanning (see Community & Standards): product repos run Snyk on PRs (snyk-test) and monitor main (snyk-monitor), and the legacy stack runs a Syft + Grype SBOM/scan pipeline that uploads findings to DefectDojo after builds.

Threat modeling is part of the operational handover. If you are developing a new product integration to Deploy App, please provide a threat model against your integration and product
